Generative Neural Feature Fields (GIRAFFE) is a scene representation framework that models individual objects within a scene using separate, compositional neural feature fields, enabling disentangled control over pose, shape, and appearance [S1, S2].

The claim is fully supported by the provided evidence. Source [S1] explicitly states that GIRAFFE assigns each object its own neural feature field MLP, takes shape and appearance latent vectors as input, and results in a disentangled latent space allowing for fine control. Source [S2] confirms that GIRAFFE represents individual objects using separate feature fields (unlike NeRF/GRAF which use a single model) and utilizes latent codes for shape and appearance to enable disentangled control over pose, shape, and appearance.
